info.title: Inlet API
info.description:
Inlet separates form definition from form rendering and response storage. Your
application fetches a published form definition, renders it however it likes, and
posts the answers back in one call.

## Collecting feedback in four calls

```bash
BASE=http://192.168.0.19:3000
KEY=ipk_your_publishable_client_key
DB=fdb_your_feedback_database_id

# 1. Read the published form
curl -s "$BASE/v1/feedback-databases/$DB/form" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"

# 2. Open a submission intent
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/v1/feedback-databases/$DB/submission-intents" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"

# 3. Optionally attach a screenshot
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/v1/feedback-databases/$DB/submission-intents/$INTENT/attachments" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Inlet-Intent-Token: $TOKEN" \
  -F questionId=el_xxxxxxxxxxxx -F file=@screenshot.png

# 4. Submit everything at once
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/v1/feedback-databases/$DB/submission-intents/$INTENT/submit" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Inlet-Intent-Token: $TOKEN" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"formVersion":1,"answers":{"el_xxxxxxxxxxxx":{"value":"It works"}}}'
```

## Two kinds of key

A **publishable client key** (`ipk_…`) is safe to embed in a browser or mobile
app. It authorizes only the four calls above.

A **secret server key** (`isk_…`) carries project Admin authority: it can read
and export submissions, manage forms, and delete data within its own project.
Keep it on a server. It is shown once, when you create it.

Send either as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. The management interface uses a
session cookie instead, obtained from `POST /v1/auth/sign-in`.

## Answers

Answers are keyed by stable question ID. The shape follows the question type in
the pinned form version, so you never repeat the type:

| Question type | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| single-select choice | `{"optionId": "op_…"}` |
| multi-select choice | `{"optionIds": ["op_…", "op_…"]}` |
| single- or multi-line text | `{"value": "…"}` |
| email | `{"value": "someone@example.com"}` |
| screenshot upload | `{"attachmentIds": ["att_…"]}` |

Omit a question entirely to leave an optional question unanswered. An empty
string never satisfies a required question.

## Retrying safely

Every submission starts with a server-issued intent, which makes retries safe.
Repeating a finalization with the same payload returns the original result;
repeating it with a different payload is a conflict and stores nothing; and a
validation failure leaves the intent usable so you can correct and resend.

## Limits

- `clientContext`: 16384 bytes serialized as UTF-8.
- Screenshots: JPEG, PNG or WebP, 10 MB and 25 megapixels per file, 5 per submission, 10 uploads per intent. Animated images are rejected.
- Every accepted image is re-encoded to WebP and brought inside 2 MB of storage, giving up quality before pixels. The width, height and bytes in an upload response describe what was stored, which may be smaller than what was sent.
- Security rate limits apply to sign-in, intent creation, uploads and
  finalization. They are not configurable.

## Errors

Every failure returns `{"error":{"code","message","details?"}}`. The `code` is
stable and safe to branch on; `details` carries `questionId` for answer problems
and `path` for request-shape problems.

version.description: Defaults to the most recent inactive version.

get.description: Elements are returned in authored order. Screenshot questions carry the platform’s accepted media types and per-file size limit (FR-046).

formVersion.description: The version the client rendered. Defaults to the active version.

post.description: Multipart form data with a `questionId` field and a `file` part. The image is validated by content, re-encoded to WebP, and returned as an attachment ID to reference at finalization.

parameters.description: "unread" narrows to what arrived since the signed-in reader last looked, and is "all" for an API key.

post.summary: Mark this list read up to now
post.description: Moves the signed-in reader’s marker, so the next read reports only what arrived after this call. Requires a session: an API key has no reader to track.

get.summary: Export submissions as JSON or CSV
get.description: Raw answers including collected email addresses, the form version, timestamp, observed IP and clientContext. Screenshots appear as stable authenticated URLs; the files are not bundled (FR-112).
Includes the definition of the form version this submission was made against, so answers can be shown with the labels the respondent saw (FR-065).

delete.summary: Permanently delete one submission and its screenshots
delete.description: Re-finalizing the submission’s intent afterwards returns 410 `submission_deleted` and exposes no answers (FR-092G).

purgedKeys.description: Screenshot objects queued for asynchronous purge (FR-027).

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Resize to this width on the way out. Omit for the stored image.

get.description: A hosted form is created, disabled, with a generated address the first time this is read.

patch.description: Enable or disable it, set a custom address, and set the branding, copy and behaviour. Every field is optional; only what is sent changes.

slug.description: A custom address. Must be unique and not reserved.

redirectUrl.description: Where to send the respondent after a successful submission.

allowedOrigins.description: Origins allowed to frame the page when embedding is "listed".

post.description: The previous address stops working immediately (FR-133).
Multipart, with a `file` part and an optional `alt` field. Validated by content and re-encoded to WebP, exactly as a screenshot is.

get.description: The webhook URL is never returned. `webhookUrlMasked` carries the host and last four characters so an operator can confirm which webhook is saved.

patch.description: Every field is optional; only what is sent changes. Setting `webhookUrl` requires a signed-in session rather than an API key. Sending `webhookUrl: null` clears it and switches notifications off.

webhookUrl.description: Write-only. Null clears it and switches notifications off. Never returned by any endpoint.

contentLevel.description: How much of a response the message carries. "link_only" sends no answer content at all; "answers" includes the answers but withholds a collected email address; "answers_with_email" includes it. Slack keeps its own copy of whatever is sent.

messageTitle.description: Replaces the default heading. May contain Slack mention syntax.

channel.description: Legacy custom integration webhooks only; Slack app webhooks ignore it.

post.description: Delivers a sample message immediately using the saved settings and reports what Slack said. The content is placeholder text, never a real response, so testing an integration never exposes a respondent.

get.description: Public. Returns the branding, the copy, and the published form when the hosted form is open. A closed hosted form returns its message and no questions.
Public, scoped to the slug. Served as WebP.

post.description: The same intent the client API issues, pinned to the same published version.

post.description: Multipart, with a `questionId` field and a `file` part. Validated, scanned and re-encoded exactly as an upload through the client API.

get.description: Public, so someone can see what they are accepting before they accept it. Reveals only the role and the scope’s name.

post.description:
Grants exactly the role and scope recorded on the invitation, whatever address the redeemer uses (FR-007), and consumes it.

Signed in already: send no body and the invitation attaches to that account.
No account yet: send an email and a password, and the account is created.

A second use, an expiry or a revocation all fail, each with its own code.
